title: Periodic Quarter-Wave Bragg Cold Mirror
scientific_hypothesis: A periodic HfO2/SiO2 quarter-wave Bragg stack with center wavelength tuned to the visible band will achieve high reflectance at 400-700 nm while maintaining high transmittance at 1530-1565 nm.
design_principle: Bragg interference from periodic high-low index pairs creates a photonic bandgap centered at the quarter-wave wavelength. L33 demonstrates this cold mirror concept with TiO2/SiO2; HfO2/SiO2 (L04, L07, L34) provides similar index contrast with better space qualification.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (10 pairs, 20 layers total)
design_variables: quarter-wave reference wavelength (tunes all layer thicknesses proportionally)
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are space-qualified materials (L07, L25, L28)
Quarter-wave thicknesses are manufacturable with standard deposition
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Bragg condition: optical thickness = λ/4 at center wavelength
Index contrast determines bandgap width and reflectance magnitude
expected_advantages: Predictable spectral position from quarter-wave wavelength
L33 validates cold mirror concept for visible-reflect/IR-transmit
known_risks: Periodic structure may have limited band-edge sharpness
Passband ripple from impedance mismatch at air interface
May not achieve both bands simultaneously with fixed pair count
execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer dielectric stack with air incidence on fused silica substrate. Stack: 10 alternating pairs of HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) (20 layers total), starting with HfO2. All layers have optical thickness equal to one quarter of a tunable reference wavelength. Optimize the reference wavelength to maximize transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band while maximizing reflectance in 400-700 nm band. Layer count fixed at 20. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Lemarchand).
